scope: One additional physical probe selected from finite candidate actions, then new RGB-D evidence and future prediction. Two rigid colored blocks; no calibrated information gain, safety guarantee or novel experiment-design algorithm.
protocol: Freeze configuration, source snapshots, initial pool, compression, probing policy and updated state packets in chronological stages. No tuning on this holdout.
Use new material/history pairs disjoint from both earlier joint-state fixtures. All initial observations use only a weak known probe.

Each pool has 49 observation callbacks and 147 design-trajectory allowance. Compare full accepted set and response8 separately. Within each state-set condition all policies get the same simulated seven-action planning bank.

Policy selection uses candidate Gaussian RGB-D summaries and simulated design response pairs only. It cannot read new actual observations, actual damage, private labels, parent config or held-out future action plan.
Summary features are known-color centroids, mean depth and foreground area at fixed heuristic scales, not calibrated sensor likelihood or pretrained representations.

Guarded policy maximizes task-weighted pair distinguishability gain over passive observation subject to maximum candidate damage added relative to passive <=0.02 and no candidate additional separation. Zero action is always a fallback. This is a finite-set heuristic, not guaranteed safety.

Trusted simulated environment reveals only each selected action's noisy RGB-D after policy sealing. Reweight/filter only original candidate states, continue the selected probe's evolved internal history, never reset/average damage or use actual hidden state.

Merge initial and new residuals with equal frame counts: arithmetic score mean and root-mean-square of RMSEs. Acceptance stays within the prior set, and failure to match is explicit rather than forced fallback.

For every physical probe action, generate its own future response targets from the resulting actual state. Compare pre/post-measurement predictions against that same action-specific target. Cross-policy raw RMSE alone is not a causal information metric.

Report actual additional damage/separation relative to passive, candidate count, unavailable predictions, MAP and nearest-set error, range width/coverage, and action frequencies. Do not equate candidate reduction with true information or calibration.

Random actions are reproducible from initial observable candidate scores and a policy seed, never pair IDs or true parameters. Three random seeds are controls on shared physical cases, not independent trials.
